reports.text: Detailed fetal anatomic survey at 21 weeks 1 day by dates. Single live intrauterine fetus, cephalic. Fetal heart rate 146 bpm. Biometry concordant with dates; estimated fetal weight at the 48th percentile. Head, face, spine, heart (four-chamber and outflow views), abdominal wall, stomach, kidneys, bladder and limbs seen and normal. Three-vessel cord. Placenta posterior, well clear of the internal os. Amniotic fluid normal. Cervix long and closed.
reports.conclusion: Normal anatomy survey. Growth appropriate. Posterior placenta, no previa.

documents.title: Anatomy scan report
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body: Ultrasound report from the patient's obstetric practice, scan date 1/2/2024, faxed for the PCP's records. Normal anatomy, appropriate growth. Filed.

documents.title: Prenatal visit 28 weeks
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Outside obstetric practice, prenatal visit 2/20/2024, 28w3d.
Feeling well, active fetal movement. No headaches, visual change, RUQ pain. Mild ankle swelling by evening, as before pregnancy, wearing compression stockings.
BP well controlled on hydrochlorothiazide; aspirin 81 mg nightly. Fundal height appropriate, FHR 140s.
1-hour glucose challenge 118 mg/dL, normal.
Tdap given today.
Plan: visits every 2 weeks from 32 weeks with BP checks; growth scan at 32 weeks; aspirin through 36 weeks; discussed induction at 39 weeks given age and chronic hypertension. Copy to PCP.

documents.title: Legs
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I'm 33 weeks now. My legs have been getting more swollen and achy since the fall and now the right one is worse than the left. OB checked my BP and urine last week and said those are fine and that legs swell in pregnancy, but with my veins and my blood pressure history I'd feel better if you looked. Standing in front of the class all day is rough.

documents.title: RE: Legs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Happy to see you. Front desk will find you a spot next week. If the right calf becomes suddenly painful, red or much bigger, or you're short of breath, go to labor and delivery or the ED that day rather than waiting for me.

orders.reason: progressive leg edema in late pregnancy with chronic hypertension; exclude cardiac cause

documents.title: Office Visit: leg swelling in pregnancy
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
48F G1 at 34w5d, EDD 5/12, prenatal care with outside OB. Chronic HTN on HCTZ, aspirin 81 through 36 weeks. Known CVI and varicose veins.

HPI: Since the fall, both lower legs swelling and aching more, now right more than left, worst late in the teaching day. No chest pain, no dyspnea at rest or lying flat, no headaches or visual change. Wears stockings most days.

Exam: vitals as charted, BP in her usual range. Gravid. Heart regular, no murmur, lungs clear, no JVD. Legs: pitting edema both sides, right a bit more, varicosities, ankle hyperpigmentation. Calves soft, not tender. Pulses intact.

A/P: Worsening edema on top of her venous insufficiency in the third trimester. OB's BP and urine checks reassuring. With her hypertension she would like a heart evaluation before delivery, and I think that's reasonable: cardiology referral, asked for a visit within 2-3 weeks. Continue stockings, elevate in the evening, sit for part of each class period if she can.

medications.drug: aspirin 81 MG Delayed Release Oral Tablet

documents.title: Prenatal visit 36 weeks
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body: Outside obstetric practice, visit 4/14/2024 (36w1d). BP controlled on HCTZ. No symptoms of preeclampsia. Growth scan at 32 weeks appropriate. Cephalic. Low-dose aspirin stopped today as planned. Induction scheduled for 5/6 at 39 weeks. Copy to PCP.

documents.title: Cardiology consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group. Visit date 4/22/2024. Requested by PCP.

Question: progressive leg edema in late pregnancy with chronic hypertension.

HPI: 48-year-old woman, G1 at 37 weeks, with hypertension on hydrochlorothiazide and obesity, who had similar leg complaints evaluated in March 2023 and was found to have venous insufficiency. Six months of increasing swelling and aching of both lower legs, worse by evening and after standing. No chest pain, no shortness of breath, no recent travel.

Meds: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily (aspirin recently stopped by OB). NKDA.
PMH: hypertension, obesity, chronic venous insufficiency, varicose veins, pregnancy. PSH: cholecystectomy.
Social: teacher, never smoker.

Exam: BP 138/86, HR 78, BMI 34. Gravid, comfortable. JVP not elevated. Heart regular, normal S1 and S2, no murmur. Lungs clear. Legs: pitting edema on both sides, more on the right; brown pigmentation around the medial malleoli; several dilated, tortuous veins on the calves. No open ulcer; healed ulcer scar over the right medial ankle.

Data: CBC normal. Creatinine 0.9. UA without protein or blood. D-dimer negative.

Impression: edema from chronic venous insufficiency with varicose veins, aggravated by late pregnancy. No clinical evidence of heart failure or another cardiac cause. Normal creatinine and no proteinuria.

Recommendations: continue graduated compression stockings and leg elevation; reassess after delivery. No cardiac testing needed. Happy to see her again if symptoms change.

documents.title: Obstetric discharge summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Regional hospital, labor and birth unit. Admitted 5/6/2024, discharged 5/9/2024.

Admitting diagnosis: pregnancy at 39w1d, advanced maternal age, chronic hypertension; scheduled induction.
Hospital course: cervical ripening and oxytocin induction. Spontaneous vaginal delivery 5/7/2024 at 03:42 of a liveborn female, 3,280 g, vigorous at birth. Estimated blood loss 350 mL. Blood pressures 120s-130s/70s-80s throughout; preeclampsia labs (CBC, creatinine, liver enzymes) normal on admission. Uncomplicated postpartum course; ambulating, voiding, pain controlled.

Discharge medications: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily (continued).
Follow-up: obstetrics in 6 weeks; BP check at home, call for BP over 150/100 or headache. Copy to PCP.

documents.title: Welcome, baby
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Andrea, I saw the hospital summary come through. I'm so glad you and your daughter are both well. Keep checking your blood pressure at home these first weeks; if it's over 150/100 or you get a bad headache, call the OB right away. Let's get you in for your physical this summer once things settle.

documents.title: RE: Welcome, baby
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you! Exhausted and happy. BPs at home 120s/80. Legs are already less puffy.

documents.title: Postpartum visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body: Outside obstetric practice, comprehensive postpartum visit 6/18/2024, 6 weeks after vaginal delivery. Recovering well. Lochia resolved. BP controlled on hydrochlorothiazide. Mood screen negative. Contraception discussed: she and her partner will use condoms; she declines hormonal methods. Return to routine gynecologic care; Pap/HPV next due 2027. Copy to PCP.

documents.title: HCTZ refill
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy request for hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg. Postpartum, OB continued it. Refilled x 90 days. Physical booked 7/23.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
48F, 11 weeks postpartum. Baby came along in the car seat and slept through it.

Interval: Uncomplicated induction and vaginal delivery 5/7. Postpartum visit with OB normal, using condoms. Sleep fragmented but mood good, partner sharing nights; PHQ-9 2. Back fine. Legs much better since delivery, still wears stockings on school days. Going back to the classroom in late August.

Meds: HCTZ 25 daily. NKDA. No tobacco; alcohol rare.

Exam: vitals as charted. Heart and lungs normal. Breasts normal. Abdomen soft, nontender, diastasis not palpable. Legs: trace ankle edema, varicosities, ankle pigmentation, healed scar right medial ankle, skin intact.

A/P
- HTN: back at her baseline on HCTZ. CMP.
- CVI: improved after delivery. Continue stockings and elevation.
- Weight: BMI about 32, near her pre-pregnancy weight. Walking with the stroller.
- Prevention: mammogram this fall (ordered). Labs today: lipids, A1c, CBC. Tdap given in pregnancy. Pap/HPV 2022, next 2027. Colonoscopy 2031. Flu and COVID in October.
BP follow-up in about 4 months.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: All normal: blood count, kidney and liver tests, potassium, A1c and cholesterol. Nice to see the blood count fully recovered after delivery.

reports.text: Bilateral screening mammogram with tomosynthesis. Compared with July 2023. Heterogeneously dense breasts, symmetric. No suspicious mass, calcification or architectural distortion.

documents.title: Mammogram 2024
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Normal screening mammogram. Patient notified.

documents.title: Flu and COVID 2024
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Trivalent flu and 2024-25 Pfizer COVID given. Tolerated. BP recorded. She'll book the BP follow-up for November at the desk.

documents.title: Heel
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Sorry I cancelled in November, the baby had a cold. Can I reschedule? Also my right heel has been killing me since the summer. First steps out of bed are like stepping on a nail, then it loosens up, then it's bad again after a day on my feet teaching. I didn't hurt it that I know of.

documents.title: RE: Heel
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: No problem at all. You're booked Tuesday 12/10 at 3:40 for your blood pressure and the heel.

documents.title: Office Visit: heel pain, HTN
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Right heel pain about 5 months, sharp, worst with the first steps in the morning and after long days standing in the classroom. No injury. Has tried different sneakers. BP fine on HCTZ, home readings 120s-130s/80s.
O: Vitals as charted. Right foot: tender over the inner heel, no swelling or redness, normal ankle motion. Legs with varicosities and trace edema, unchanged.
A/P:
1. Right heel pain, sounds like plantar fascia. She'd like orthopedics to look and decide on any imaging; referral placed. Meanwhile calf stretches before getting out of bed.
2. HTN controlled. BMP today. Continue HCTZ.
3. CVI stable with stockings.
Physical next summer.
